subject: VPC fee allocations and on-prem SLA credit path
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Claire Ramos <claire@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC fee allocations and on-prem SLA credit path

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for taking time on the call earlier. Attached is a first-pass SOW and a compact pricing workbook so Novamed can see how platform fees break down across 1-, 2-, and 3-year options. High level thinking from our side:

- Option A: Standard platform fee amortized monthly over the contract term (3-year example in the workbook). Lower upfront, predictable ARR.
- Option B: Split model — smaller upfront platform fee + committed throughput credit pool (consumable against token usage). This reduces initial cash and preserves unit economics for both sides.
- Migration credit proposal: one-time engineering credit to offset on-prem integration effort (we've put a placeholder in the workbook).

Attachments: Novamed-SOW-draft.pdf (PDF, 210KB), redwood_pricing_workbook.csv (CSV, 95KB)

Can you confirm which approach is closest to what procurement expects? If you like, we can produce a tailored example that maps Novamed's forecasted node counts to the committed credit model.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Quick call to pick A vs B (30m)
2) We finalize SOW and the migration-credit line item
3) DocuSign for signature

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

From: Claire Ramos <claire@novamed.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC fee allocations and on-prem SLA credit path

Hi Sean —

Appreciate the documents. A couple of immediate asks from procurement/IT:

- Can you show an example where platform fee is converted into a 12-month operational retainer + a support tier (we prefer OPEX over large multi-year capital-like fees).
- We need clearer language on the migration credit: is it a one-time dollar offset, or an engineering-hour estimate?
- If we later decide to move a portion to Redwood Dedicated, are there upgrade credits for the committed throughput?

I can loop our procurement lead (procure@novamed.com) if helpful. Would also like a simple line-by-line table that we can drop into our procurement comparison sheet.

Thanks,
Claire Ramos
Head of Partnerships, Novamed
claire@novamed.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Claire Ramos <claire@novamed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC fee allocations and on-prem SLA credit path

Hi all — looping Karthik for the licensing/support nuance. Sean — good framing. Claire — answering your bullets and proposing a specific path that matches Novamed's ask for OPEX-friendly treatment:  

1) Platform fee as 12-month operational retainer + consumable credits
   - We can offer a 12-month retainer equal to ~40% of the 3-year amortized platform fee which covers platform governance, minor upgrades, and telemetry retention.
   - Committed throughput credits are purchased in advance and drawn down; any unused credits will be eligible for a 6-month carry-forward (not refundable).

2) Migration credit mechanics
   - Proposal: one-time migration credit of $75,000 applied against the first invoice, documented as an implementation discount (not a separate refund). We can alternatively structure as up to 300 engineering hours at our standard implementation rate if you prefer hour accounting.

3) Upgrade path to Dedicated
   - We can provide a 50% credit on the remaining committed credits at the point of transition (applies to unused credit balance only). That gives you upside if you later choose dedicated capacity.

Attachments: pricing_scenarios.xlsx (Excel, 85KB) — includes 3 worked examples (12-month retainer, 24-month split, 36-month amortized).

Related links: HubSpot deal NOVA-2026-0047: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

If this looks reasonable, Sean — I suggest we:
- Produce the line-item table Claire requested
- Add the migration credit clause to the SOW (one-line)
- Prepare DocuSign envelope with the chosen term

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: VPC fee allocations and on-prem SLA credit path

Hi Claire —

Thanks — based on Marissa's proposals below, here's a concise, actionable revision we can put in an updated SOW and pricing table: 

Summary proposal (for Novamed review)
- Term: 12 months (option to renew)
- Platform: 12-month operational retainer = 40% of standard 36-month amortized platform fee (invoiced monthly)
- Committed credits: Upfront purchase covering predicted throughput (drawn down monthly); unused credits carry forward up to 6 months
- Migration credit: $75,000 one-time credit applied to first invoice (or up to 300 implementation hours at customer's choice)
- Upgrade to Dedicated: 50% credit on unused committed credits at transition
- Support: Standard Support included; SLA Premium (24/7 oncall + 1-hour P1 response) available as a $x/month add-on — we can price that after you confirm expected P1 frequency.

Next steps
1) Confirm you want the 12-month retainer + committed credits path (reply-in-thread)
2) We'll drop the updated line-by-line table into the SOW and send DocuSign for signature (I’ll include the migration credit language)
3) Procurement signs and we kick off onboarding (we'll schedule an implementation checklist call)

If Novamed wants, we can run a quick worked example mapping your FY27 forecast to committed credits (takes 1 business day).

Would you be able to confirm by July 30 so we can hold the proposed migration credit in the quote?

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
